scope: Genesis 1:1-3 and John 1:1-3; native Strong's links on verse 1 for BSB and KJV only

BSB.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.
And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.

KJV1769.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

WEBSTER1833.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep: and the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

ASV1901.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
And the earth was waste and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep: and the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

BSB.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was with God in the beginning.
Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.

KJV1769.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The same was in the beginning with God.
All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

WEBSTER1833.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The same was in the beginning with God.
All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

ASV1901.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The same was in the beginning with God.
All things were made through him; and without him was not anything made that hath been made.

H7225.concise_definition: the first, in place, time, order or rank (specifically, a firstfruit)

H430.concise_definition: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative

H1254.concise_definition: (absolutely) to create; (qualified) to cut down (a wood), select, feed (as formative processes)

H8064.concise_definition: the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve)

H776.concise_definition: the earth (at large, or partitively a land)

G746.concise_definition: (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank)

G3056.concise_definition: something said (including the thought); by implication, a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ)

G2532.concise_definition: and, also, even, so then, too, etc.; often used in connection (or composition) with other particles or small words

G4314.concise_definition: a preposition of direction; forward to, i.e. toward (with the genitive case, the side of, i.e. pertaining to; with the dative case, by the side of, i.e. near to; usually with the accusative case, the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the destination of the relation, i.e. whither or for which it is predicated)

G2316.concise_definition: a deity, especially (with G3588) the supreme Divinity; figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very
